newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call rates climb on month-end pressures.
newsitem.headline: German call rates climb on month-end pressures.

text.p: German overnight call rates crept higher to trade near 3.20 percent on Thursday as traders readied for the month-end reserve period.
Traders said banks were trying to get their reserve positions in order so that they would not have to borrow from the Bundesbank's more expensive Lombard lending facility over the weekend.
Some traders said rates could fall as early as Friday.
"When everybody like a flock of sheep meets reserve targets, I could imagine with a view to balances that tomorrow there could suddenly be too much liquidity."
Credit institutions held 44.7 billion marks with Bundesbank on Wednesday, leaving the average for the month so far at 40.7 billion marks.
No significant amount of funds was borrowed from the Lombard lending window.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.19583 percent on Thursday morning compared with 3.09358 percent the day before.
